explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/431: "Are there two infinite sets A and B such that A+B agrees with the set of prime numbers up to finitely many exceptions?" (Ostmann's inverse Goldbach problem; "the answer is surely no"). The Lean statement is ¬∃ A B : Set ℕ, both infinite, with A + B =ᶠ[cofinite] {n | n.Prime}; EventuallyEq of sets along the cofinite filter means membership agrees for all but finitely many n, i.e. finite symmetric difference — exactly "agrees up to finitely many exceptions". The negation encodes the expected/claimed "no" answer. The "solved" status relies on the cited OpenAI preprint; I checked that the linked Lean file exists at the pinned commit and contains `twoInfiniteSummandsImpossible` ("two infinite nonnegative summands cannot give the primes outside a finite initial interval"). The erdosproblems.com page I fetched still showed the problem as open, so the status is ahead of the site, but the statement itself is faithful.
